metadata.title: Stock Market Today: Dow Futures Drop as Apple Sinks After Earnings; Chip Stocks Rebound as AMD Results Loom

content.text:
Stock futures are pointing to a mixed open for major indexes Tuesday as investors digest a flurry of earnings reports and turn their attention to the midterm elections.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 0.6% recently, while S&P 500 futures slipped 0.1% and tech-heavy Nasdaq futures rose 0.4%. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite have closed lower in each of the past three sessions amid a tech stock sell-off sparked in part by disappointing earnings reports.
This morning, shares of Dow component Apple (AAPL) were down 4% after the tech giant reported better-than-expected quarterly numbers but pointed to weakening margins. Palantir (PLTR) shares were down 7% ahead of the opening bell even as the data analytics software maker topped Wall Street estimates with its results and issued a rosy forecast.
Chip stocks are rebounding this morning from big losses, as investors await quarterly numbers from Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), due after the closing bell. AMD shares, which have lost nearly 20% of their value over the previous three sessions, were up 3% in recent premarket trading. Intel (INTC) shares were up 4% this morning, after falling 37% during their three-day slump. Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO) were each up roughly 2% recently.
Market participants are bracing for the results of the midterm elections amid uncertainty about what a potential shift of the balance of power in Congress could mean for government spending, regulation and more. (You can read Investopedia's analysis of how the election results could affect the economy here.)
Meanwhile, WTI crude oil futures were up 0.9% at $97.30 per barrel in recent trading, after the U.S. benchmark plunged 8% yesterday amid hopes that the U.S. would seek a diplomatic solution to the Iran war rather than launch new strikes after the midterms.
Gold futures were down 1.1% at $3,925 an ounce, moving back toward levels hit last Friday, when the price of the precious metal hit its lowest level since September of last year. Bitcoin was holding steady at $77,300.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which affects the interest rates charged on all sorts of consumer loans, rose to 4.94% from 4.91% at yesterday's close.
